long_biography.plain_text:
Cheton entered a business begun by his mother, who opened her first establishment in the Drôme in 1962 and later acquired another in Grasse. He took the reins in the late 1980s and developed a high-service model combining residential care with restaurant, hotel, medical and social provision under one operating system.

Growth came first through new facilities and then through acquisitions, extensions and conversions. Cheton pushed the company into Belgium, Switzerland, Italy and Spain while retaining a strong role in designing, building and operating its properties. A 2019 capital reorganisation brought Naxicap Partners and Ardian into the group, with Cheton remaining its largest minority shareholder. His later companies have focused on investment management, real estate and hotel operations.

uncertainties.detail: Investment sources often call Cheton the founder of Emera because he created the modern group and its operating model. Specialist sector history supplies an earlier layer: his mother opened one establishment and acquired another before he assumed leadership. Inherited and expanded therefore describes the wealth mechanism more accurately than Self-made or Inherited alone, while Operator captures his decades of transformative work.

Strong sources variously date Emera's creation to 1987 or 1988, while specialist history places Cheton's assumption of the family activity in 1989. The biographies avoid asserting one exact corporate founding year and instead use the well-supported late-1980s transition, preserving the distinction between predecessor establishments and the modern group.

Cheton's fortune-creating industry is unambiguously Healthcare. Sector analysis reports his exit from the remaining Emera stake in early 2025. Current French records then show substantial investment and holding vehicles, property companies and a new hotel-operating mandate. Finance & Investments is used for Primary Industry because the private investment platform is established and broader; the hotel activity is very recent and is not yet evidenced as the dominant current wealth base.

CCBB, Philoanne, Foncière Roy René and FILO establish current management roles but do not make every company asset Cheton's personal property. Béatrice Cheton is explicitly a co-manager or officer in several records, and Emera historically included other family and management shareholders. The dossier identifies platforms and roles without allocating undocumented individual ownership percentages or transferring relatives' roles to Claude.
